scenes.setup: The ferry has docked late with the festival's lamp oil, and a big crowd is waiting on the dock.

options.text: Take the engine apart and find the fault
Measure the tides and work out what is wrong
Paint a bright sign to cheer up the waiting crowd
Sing with the waiting children to keep them calm

scenes.lit: The oil is ashore, and the harbour lamp catches. The water shines back.

scenes.setup: The old bridge by the lamp post is worn, and the festival crowd will need to cross it soon.

options.text: Fit the planks exactly as the plan shows
Study how old arches stand, then sketch a better one
Design a striking new bridge shape and test that it stands
Take charge of the schedule and the money for the repair

scenes.lit: Lantern-bearers stream across, and the old arch glows.

scenes.setup: The tower clock that tells the lane when to light its lamps is running wrong, and visitors are arriving for the festival.

options.text: Climb up and trace the broken gear by hand
Work out from the pattern of missed chimes what went wrong
Decorate the clock face to welcome visitors
Start a repair log and organise who does each job

scenes.lit: The tower strikes dusk. Every window in the lane lights at once.

scenes.setup: The orchard folk promised sweet juice to every lamp-bearer, but the early harvest is piling up faster than they can cope.

options.text: Run the press and keep every crate stacked right
Try blends of apples to invent a new juice flavour
Teach visiting children to make juice, with games
Sell the juice and keep the accounts tidy

scenes.lit: The orchard is calm. Its lamp swings among the apple trees.

scenes.setup: Fog has settled on the pass, the signal lamp is dim, and festival travellers are feeling their way through.

options.text: Fix the broken signal lamp so people can see it
Map where the fog thickens, and find out why
Welcome the lost travellers and get them moving together
Count everyone through and keep the group in order

scenes.lit: A thin gold line cuts the fog. The pass has its light, and the way is clear.

scenes.setup: The bazaar opens at dusk for the festival, the one place the whole road meets, and the stall lent to you is empty apart from a strange old machine in the corner.

options.text: Build a sturdy stall and set it up to the plan
Examine a strange old machine and imagine what it did
Call to the crowd and make every visitor feel at home
Sort the stock by size and label every shelf

scenes.lit: The bazaar glows, and a lamp hangs overhead, warm as a cup of tea.

scenes.setup: A wide river lies across the road, and a tired group of lamp-bearers has stopped to rest on the bank.

options.text: Build a raft and work out which wood floats best
Sketch a boat nobody has imagined, then try it
Look after tired travellers and gently get them going again
Lead the camp meeting and make sure everyone is heard

scenes.lit: The group is rested and ready for the crossing. The lamp's reflection drifts downstream.

scenes.setup: The great loom that weaves the festival banners is creaking, and market day is almost here.

options.text: Repair the loom and keep it working to the pattern
Design a pattern that tells the town's story
Coach a shy weaver to show their work with pride
Check every roll of cloth and store it neatly

scenes.lit: Banners hang above the street, and a lamp lights behind them.

scenes.setup: A group wants to reach the cliff top by evening to light the highest lamp, and the glassy cliffs are glowing strangely.

options.text: Rope down the cliff and test the rock as you go
Watch the cliff light change and work out why it glows
Organise the climbers into teams with a clear timetable
Check the safety gear, then brief the group on the plan

scenes.lit: The highest lamp is lit. The cliffs shine like glass for miles.

scenes.setup: A load of lamp oil has spilled at the market, two traders are arguing, and a crowd is gathering.

options.text: Haul and stack the barrels so they stay put
Help a lost trader find family and get others to help
Negotiate a fair deal between the two arguing traders
Weigh and record every sack, then pack the cart

scenes.lit: The market hums, and its lamp is lit above the stalls.

scenes.setup: A clear night is coming for the festival, visitors are climbing the hill to watch the stars come out, and the hill's stargazing club hopes to welcome them.

options.text: Chart the stars and wonder what they mean
Paint the night sky and notice how it changes
Show visitors around and gently persuade them to join the club
Run the club night and make everyone feel included

scenes.lit: The hill lamp lifts its light into the dark, and the sky answers.

scenes.setup: The garden that grows the festival's sweet lamp-herbs is overgrown, and the season is turning.

options.text: Experiment with soil and seed to grow healthier plants
Shape a garden that makes people feel peaceful
Teach children to care for the plants, with stories
Label every herb and keep the beds in neat rows

scenes.lit: The beds breathe, and the lamp smells of rain and mint.

scenes.setup: An old printing press has been found in a cellar, and the quarter wants to use it for the festival.

options.text: Investigate how the old press makes its mark
Design a new letter style and test how readable it is
Pitch a new newspaper and set the plan and prices
Proofread every page and keep the print run on schedule

scenes.lit: Ink and paper fill the quarter, and a lamp lights above the cellar door.

scenes.setup: Many travellers have come to the healing house to rest before the festival, and some are unwell tonight.

options.text: Test the water supply to find what is making people ill
Comfort the patients and organise helpers for the night
Run the clinic and make sure everyone is seen kindly
Keep the medicine store counted and in perfect order

scenes.lit: The house settles into calm. A steady lamp burns in the window.

scenes.setup: The square where the lamps will gather is still bare, and the festival begins at dusk.

options.text: Create the welcome arch with a story in its design
Perform with the visitors so they feel part of it
Run the festival: set the stalls, the prices and the plan
Keep permits and timings in order and keep stallholders informed

scenes.lit: The square is ready, and its lamp glows over the cobbles.

story.title: The Night of Lamps
story.premise: Once a year, every lamp on the old road is lit and the lighthouse at its end shines out to sea, so that anyone far from home can find the way back. This year the lamplighter has gone. The towns have been waiting. Jyo, a firefly who remembers every lamp, has found you.
story.mission: Walk the road, help each town in the way you would most gladly spend an evening, and light its lamp. When enough lamps burn, the lighthouse will shine and show you the doors that open for you.

first: This is the first dark lamp. I have waited a long time for someone to carry the lantern.
early: Another town, another lamp. The road is starting to remember itself.
The lamps ahead are watching us. Let us not keep them waiting.
middle: Look back. The lamps behind us make a line of light.
The hills are glowing now. Keep going.
Can you feel it? The road is warmer than it was.
Every lamp you light makes the next one easier to find.
late: The air smells of salt. The lighthouse is somewhere ahead.
The road is almost bright. A few dark corners left.
We have come a long way together, you and I.
Nearly there. The sea is listening.
return: This lamp has flickered, as if it wanted another look. What would you do this time?

story.outro: The lighthouse is lit. The old lamplighter left a note by its lamp: 'A lamp burns best for hands that like the work.' Whatever you chose along the way, every lamp caught. This is the light you carry.
